patch_description:
This candidate combines the strongest elements from the prior programs. The 3-parameter fully-shared-per-block design (RY tilt on all qubits, ZZ ring entangler on all 8 edges, RZ phase on all qubits) achieved the best combined score with only 20 total parameters (18 circuit + 2 readout), full accuracy (train/val/test = 1.00), zero generalization gap, and the best parameter_efficiency_mean (0.05) among all candidates. The other variants (10-param/block with 62 total params, and 5-param/block with 32 total params) added more parameters without any accuracy or convergence benefit — they simply spent more parameter budget to reach the same perfect performance level, which is penalized by the parameter-economy objective. 

The crossover here keeps the winning ultra-compact ANSATZ_SPEC (3 shared params: ry_shared, zz_shared, rz_shared) as the core design, since it already saturates achievable accuracy while minimizing parameters. This maximizes the "parameter economy" reward while preserving full entangling connectivity (complete ring of ZZ gates spanning all 8 qubits) and collective single-qubit control (shared RY tilt + shared RZ phase), which was shown empirically sufficient for the classification task. All other fixed training/dataset/readout code is preserved unchanged as required.

Design justification for keeping the "tilt+twist+phase" pattern but not the symmetry-breaking or asymmetric-pair extensions: those additions (break_ry/break_rz on qubit 0, or zz_even/zz_odd splitting) increase the parameter count by 60-70% without any measurable accuracy or convergence gain in the given metrics table — so the additional capacity is unused/wasted budget under this metric.
